in_text_mentions: rdiograms. Further imaging included a head CT venogram which showed convexity of bilateral cavernous sinuses with filling defects indicative of bilateral cavernous sinus thromboses. Coronal T1 postcontrast MRI demonstrated an enlarged and rounded appearance of the cavernous sinus with heterogeneous enhancement, consistent with cavernous sinus thrombosis (see Figure 3). MRI of the sella turcica also showed a filling defect within the left internal jugular vein (IJV) from the jugular foramen to the level of C1 with preservation of flow distal and proximal, suspicious for nonocclusive thrombosis.

e developed hallucinations, memory loss, urinary and fecal incontinence, and gait instability. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI showing bilateral cavernous sinus thrombosis and enlarged thrombosed superior orbital veins, classic manifestations of septic cavernous sinus thrombosis. B: Contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrating filling defects in the bilateral cavernous sinus, the hallmark radiological sign of septic cavernous sinus thrombosis. C: T1-weighted contrast MRI showing low signal intensity within the transverse sinus and sigmoid sinus, indicating thrombus extension from the cavernous sinus, a recognized complication of septic cavernous sinus thrombosis. D: T1-weighted contrast MRI showing low signal intensity within the transverse sinus and sigmoid sinus, demonstrating venous thrombus extension consistent with septic cavernous sinus thrombosis.
